newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary bank run shows over-sensitivity - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Hungary bank run shows over-sensitivity - analysts.

text.p: Panic withdrawals from Hungary's Postabank may indicate the financial sector's over-sensitivity to rumours in a country where people have little experience in financial matters, the Hungarian Banking Association said.

"Things like (the run on Postabank) occur everywhere -- this does not show a weakness in the Hungarian banking system," general secretary Miklos Pulai said. "But this may indicate a weakness in the whole financial culture."
Customers of Postabank, Hungary's second largest bank, started a run on branches on Friday after rumours spread that the bank may become insolvent.
Government and central bank officials assured depositors that Postabank was able to pay out deposits, however they were still puzzled on Monday over what started the panic.

"How the panic began and whether it was something organised, as suggested in the press, I don't know. We still don't know what caused it," Imre Tarafas, president of the State Money and Capital Market Supervision told Reuters.
Postabank said on Monday it will ask the police to investigate the possibility of deliberate rumour-spreading.
Pulai pointed out that this was largest ever run on a Hungarian bank but not the first time rumours had triggered alarm in the banking sector.

Two years ago, just before the government launched a radical economic austerity package to cut soaring budget and current account deficits, a rumour that retail foreign currency accounts would be frozen, created a large wave of withdrawals.
"(Hungary's) financial culture is not developed enough, and hysteria can grip (banking customers)," he said.
However, he added that runs on banks triggered by unconfirmed news was not unknown even in developed countries.
"I don't think Hungary is extraordinary in seeing (large-scale panic) once in ten years."
Hungary has had a head start on other post communist banking sectors as its 1980s communist government introduced commercial banks as early as 1986 to replace its centralised banking system.

Recapitalisation, technological development, the appearance of foreign banks, bank cards, ATM's and sophisticated services, are considered to have raised the Hungarian banking system to one of the leaders in central and eastern Europe.
However, the public lacked confidence in what the financial authorities say, analysts said.
"If the Finance Ministry, the banking authority and the central bank say that there is no problem with a bank, people should believe it," Daewoo Securities analyst Zoltan Varadi said.
By Monday the general alarm appeared to be subsiding as media reports said queues in front of Postabank branches were shorter than on previous days.

On Friday and Saturday some 21 billion forints ($119 million) were withdrawn from Postabank, which said it had access to immediately liquid assets of 70 billion forints, while its total retail deposits totalled some 200 billion forints.
